introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2021. Time allowed: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.
incertitudes: Question 4 : « at an angle of 110 degrees to another force » est lu comme l'angle entre les directions des deux forces représentées à partir du même point (110 degrés entre elles) ; le sujet n'imprime pas de schéma. Avec cette lecture R = 52,3 N. Si l'angle de 110 degrés désignait l'angle extérieur (70 degrés entre les forces), R vaudrait 73,9 N. Le sujet imprime « (5 marks) » pour la question.

questions.enonce_markdown: A force of $40\ \mathrm{N}$ acts on a body at an angle of $110^\circ$ to another force of $50\ \mathrm{N}$ acting on the same body. Calculate the resultant force acting on the body. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The angle between the directions of the two forces (drawn from the same point) is $\theta = 110^\circ$.

**Magnitude (cosine rule / parallelogram of forces).**
$$R^2 = F_1^2 + F_2^2 + 2F_1F_2\cos\theta = 40^2 + 50^2 + 2(40)(50)\cos110^\circ$$
$$R^2 = 1600 + 2500 + 4000\times(-0.3420) = 4100 - 1368.1 = 2731.9\ \mathrm{N^2}$$
$$R = \sqrt{2731.9} = 52.3\ \mathrm{N}.$$

**Direction.** Take the $50\ \mathrm{N}$ force along the $x$-axis and the $40\ \mathrm{N}$ force at $110^\circ$ to it:
$$R_x = 50 + 40\cos110^\circ = 50 - 13.68 = 36.32\ \mathrm{N},\qquad R_y = 40\sin110^\circ = 37.59\ \mathrm{N}.$$
Check: $\sqrt{36.32^2 + 37.59^2} = 52.3\ \mathrm{N}$.
$$\tan\alpha = \frac{R_y}{R_x} = \frac{37.59}{36.32} = 1.035 \;\Rightarrow\; \alpha = 46.0^\circ$$
measured from the $50\ \mathrm{N}$ force (that is $110 - 46.0 = 64.0^\circ$ from the $40\ \mathrm{N}$ force).

**The resultant force is $52.3\ \mathrm{N}$, at $46.0^\circ$ to the $50\ \mathrm{N}$ force.**
